pillar_reactions.evidence: The most engaged pillar reception in the batch. He took written notes and read the whole thing back accurately and unprompted: 'so I guess the two modalities is training mobility. I got three to four times doing 30 minutes per session... Mobility versus flexibility, three to six months, and then the feedback videos for Trevor still can adjust and correct.' He reacted positively to the time commitment — 'Oh, that's really good' — and engaged substantively with the mobility-versus-flexibility distinction, connecting it to the Stretch Lab sessions he already attends: 'I really need to get on a regimented stretching program.' The only reservation he raised was age-appropriateness, which is logged as an objection.

Asked two practical questions. First on the 80/20 split — 'what is 80-20 nutrition training?... I guess the whole program, what is more important' — which he answered largely himself with the standard gym framing. Second on cost: 'for the nutrition part, is a lot of the map or the road guide for that all stuff you got to purchase or is there like stuff that's included?' He was reassured by the no-macro-tracking positioning: 'I thought it was going to have to do something with, you know, watching your macros and all that stuff.' He also volunteered that he had been consistent with supplementation while training last year and stopped when he stopped training.

Probed the one thing that matters to a preserver — what happens after the programme ends: 'after you're done teaching the fish, what if like you hit, if someone hits a plateau, am I going be able to like reach back to Trevor or to a community where I can get some feedback?' Answered with the community. He had already named the gap the pillar addresses, unprompted: 'There's no accountability and there's no feedback' when working from free information. He also described his own portability plan for it — kettlebells in the boot of the car, trained wherever the shift puts him.

anchors.raw: I was out of shape. So I said, you know, let me go hire a personal trainer, which I dropped 500 bucks. And it was money well spent because I got in as a supplemental... I just went and hired the same personal trainer again
anchors.competitor: A local personal trainer, hired twice
anchors.note: The strongest supportive anchor in this batch and it was never used. He has paid for coaching twice, for a specific outcome, and describes it in his own words as money well spent — plus it worked, twice, and secured him a job he had waited six years for. That is a proven willingness to buy coaching against a defined result. It surfaced only incidentally at 00:32:14 and the rep did not connect it to the offer. Note the reference price is $500, which cuts the other way on magnitude.

anchors.raw: I have $1,000 that I got to take care of this month for these guys that I joined up for helping me to use my VA loan to get a place... I got involved with them back in January, and it was like six grand for their, for their program
anchors.competitor: A credit-repair / VA loan facilitation programme
anchors.note: The decisive number and it was disclosed voluntarily. He is already servicing a roughly $6,000 high-ticket programme at $1,000 a month for two more months, in pursuit of a goal he rates above this one — buying a home so his wife can join him from the Philippines. Against roughly $2,000 monthly disposable income, adding $1,200 a month puts him $200 in deficit for the first two months. It also establishes that he buys high-ticket programmes on instalments, which cuts both ways.

anchors.raw: we have these things called, well, we have these stretch sessions through this company called Stretch Lab... In fact, right before my chiropractic appointment, I came from a stretch session with Stretch Lab and stuff. And I always feel good after
anchors.competitor: Stretch Lab and chiropractic care, both covered by employer benefits
anchors.note: He already receives mobility and manual therapy at no personal cost through a benefits package he describes as 'real good'. The rep handled this well — drawing the mobility-versus-flexibility distinction to differentiate rather than dismiss — which is the sharpest positioning move he made on any call in this batch.

anchors.raw: It's seven grand this past December, too, to get my van back on the road and stuff... That kind of hit me pretty hard.
anchors.note: A recent $7,000 unplanned expense on top of the credit-repair obligation. Together these establish that his liquidity is thin and recently drained, which is the profile the payment plan was then built on top of.

anchors.raw: there's also a lot of noise, right? There's so much information out there and a lot of it's good information, but then... it's like hit and miss
anchors.note: Rare in this corpus: the rep raised the free alternative and the prospect argued against it himself, then reinforced it later — 'if I wanted to get a six pack, I wouldn't be able to get it if I watched videos on YouTube... those can only take you so far. There's no accountability and there's no feedback.' The free route was neutralised without the rep having to do anything.

unmet_demand.want: Evidence that the programme works for people in their late fifties and beyond — he asked directly whether a coach in his forties can programme for a 58-year-old, and said he wanted to see testimonials from that age group
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing was shown or named. The answer was an assertion about ten years of experience and 'all age groups, of all demographics', followed by 'At the end of the day, we're all human.' Age-group social proof is the single most obvious asset for a prospect whose whole thesis is preservation, and either it does not exist in usable form or the rep did not have it to hand.

unmet_demand.want: Programming that is safe for an acute bilateral lumbar sprain sustained a month earlier and still under chiropractic management
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never established. No question was asked about diagnosis, severity, current restriction or clinical clearance, and there is no described mechanism for the programme to coordinate with a treating clinician. The back was instead absorbed into the pitch as a limitation the baseline assessment would account for.

unmet_demand.want: Conditioning specific to the job — handling the physical rigours of longshore work, the vehicle vibration, and the periodic physical agility test the role depends on
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This is the entire reason he called and it was acknowledged in general terms only. He has previously paid a trainer specifically to mimic the agility test, so he knows what job-specific programming looks like and what it is worth. No capability, protocol or precedent was offered.

unmet_demand.want: A monthly payment level a $2,000 disposable income can actually carry alongside an existing $1,000-a-month commitment
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The longest plan available was six payments, and stretching to six was itself presented as an exception. At $1,200 a month the structure consumes 60% of his stated disposable income and exceeds it outright for the first two months. There is no twelve-month or longer in-house option, and finance-partner routes require the credit he does not have.

unmet_demand.want: Continued access after the programme ends if he plateaus
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered adequately with the community, and he accepted it. Recorded only because for a preserver — someone buying maintenance of function rather than a transformation — the post-programme question is the purchase decision, and it was handled in one line at the end rather than positioned as a pillar.
